q1_issues.issue: 'first-quarter' is attached as a Time role on 'profit', a non-event noun, where Time attaches to event witnesses or event-denoting nouns; the compound rule would instead fuse first_quarter_profit with genus (Inheritance first_quarter_profit profit), the noun-modifier left unexposed as in night_shift.

The per-share figure is stored as a second Measure on the same entity under the same 'profit' scale as the dollar total, so a rate (cent_per_share) and a money amount read as two competing values of one dimension.

q2_gaps: appositive / equivalence 'or' ('$13.1 million, or 22 cents per share' — one amount restated, not a disjunction) — the disjunction section treats every 'or' as introducing a disjunct and would emit an (Or ...)

a participial post-modifier that is itself a stative locative ('the company, based in Winston-Salem') — the reduced-relative rule prescribes an event with the modified noun in a role, while the stative-locative rule prescribes a bare LocatedIn and no event
notes: The appositive taking the host clause's past wrapper — (Past (LocatedIn sk_company_1 winston_salem)) — follows the mechanical tense rule, and winston_salem plus its Name string are right for a hyphenated proper noun. Expanding '$13.1 million' to 13100000 is numeral normalization rather than a unit conversion, so it stays inside the rules.
